title: Harlem as a happy place and Bert Williams' routines
summary: Green recalls Paul Robeson and Bert Williams in Harlem and Williams' hole-card and crossing-the-street routines.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, yes. Especially in Harlem, yes. See, they had -- see, those places were -- well, it was kind of mysterious, because Harlem was famous in those days for being a happy place. There was always a lot of laughter going on. And there were some great people up there, you know, in Harlem, you know. Sometimes there was Paul Robeson. You know he was great. And there was Bert Williams. He was great, you see.

Let me -- as long as you got onto Bert Williams, I'm particularly taking an interest in him because of his sense of humor, his unique sense of humor. And if there's any routines that you remember of him, I think that that would be very interesting for you to tell. (Recording interruption) What sort of -- if you don't remember the particular routines, what were the names of some of the songs he used to do?
Well, he did something -- he did something about a hole card. Ace up the sleeves. He did something about, 'Officer, can you show me how to cross to the other side of the street?'
